newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens chief says nuclear business stays.
newsitem.headline: Siemens chief says nuclear business stays.

text.p: Siemens AG chief executive Heinrich von Pierer said on Thursday the company had no plans to leave the nuclear energy business in the foreseeable future, despite some public opposition to the technology in Germany.
The world's increasing population was quickly raising demand for energy, he said at a celebration of the company's 150th birthday.

Atomic energy did not produce carbon dioxide emissions that are suspected of raising temperatures in the earth's atmosphere, von Pierer said. At the same time, renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power were not yet ready to replace nuclear plants economically, he said.
"If someone at the end of the 20th century wants to talk about an alternative source of energy, then that can only mean atomic energy," he said.
In the first half of 1996/97, Siemens' KWU power generation unit reported sales fell 28 percent to 2.4 billion marks while orders fell 20 percent to four billion marks.
